top_story: Storm damage in Gaza has turned prolonged displacement into an acute survival crisis: after floods wrecked about 70,000 tents on 9 November, more than 940,000 displaced Palestinians remain exposed to cold, waterlogged ground, and the delayed delivery of 150,000 replacement tents is now a life-threatening bottleneck. The emergency is not only meteorological but political, because the collapse of shelter capacity deepens public anger over the restriction and delay of basic supplies while rescue services remain overwhelmed. In Saudi Arabia, the sentencing of a Kenyan migrant worker to 100 lashes for giving birth outside marriage underscores a parallel regional pattern in which vulnerable non-citizens bear the sharpest edge of state power. The immediate takeaway is that across these cases, weak protection for displaced people and migrant laborers is converting administrative and judicial decisions into direct human harm.
